physicalNotes: Radius 0.08475332 Jupiter radii from Niraula et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..172N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....160..172N/abstract): 6,059.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00254 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Niraula et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..172N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NIRAULA_ET_AL__2020): P 3.1443189 d
sources.shape: Niraula et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..172N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NIRAULA_ET_AL__2020): a/R* 25.72; Niraula et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..172N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NIRAULA_ET_AL__2020): inclination 88.74 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Niraula et al. 2020 (2020AJ....160..172N), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname NIRAULA_ET_AL__2020): transit mid-time 2457990.862 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 7 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
